rejected.title: Tectonic forces and mountains
card: The Earth's crust is broken into large pieces called plates. They move very slowly, only a few centimetres a year.
Where two plates push together, the rock at the edges is squeezed. Layers of rock can be crumpled and folded upwards over millions of years to form mountains.
Where one plate is forced down under another, rock can melt deep below. This melted rock can rise to the surface and erupt, forming volcanoes.
The Himalayas formed where the Indian Plate pushed into the Eurasian Plate. The mountains are still rising slowly today.
rejected.remember: Plates move slowly. Where they push together, rock can fold up into mountains and volcanoes can form.

a.q: What builds mountains where two plates of the Earth's crust push together?
opts: Squeezing that folds rock layers upwards
Wind and rain wearing rock layers away
Rivers dropping layers of sediment
Plates pulling apart as the crust cools
a.why: Pushing plates squeeze the rock at their edges, folding the layers upwards into mountains over millions of years. Wind and rain wear rock down, so they lower the land rather than build mountains.
a.clue: Think about what squeezing does to layers of rock.

b.q: Scientists find that a mountain range has formed where two plates are pushing together. Which statement about how it formed is correct?
opts: It built up slowly over millions of years
It formed suddenly in a single year
It formed when plates pulled far apart
It formed because rivers piled up sediment
b.why: Plates move only a few centimetres a year, so folding rock into mountains takes millions of years. Rivers can drop sediment, but here it is the pushing plates that fold rock up into mountains.
b.clue: Plates move only a few centimetres a year.

wants.why: It shows how pushing plates fold rock up into mountains.
